KIVIXA PRIVACY POLICY
Last Updated: May 2026

1. OUR PRIVACY PHILOSOPHY
Privacy is not a "feature" of Kivixa; it is the foundation. Our architecture is designed so that your data is never collected, stored on our servers, or sold to third parties.

2. DATA COLLECTION & PROCESSING
Personal Information: We do not require an account to use Kivixa. We do not collect your name, email address, or phone number.

Usage Data (Telemetry): Kivixa does not include telemetry or "phone home" tracking. We do not know how often you use the app or which features you prefer.

Crash Reporting: Optional crash reports may be generated by your operating system (Android/Windows). These are governed by your OS privacy settings and are not directly collected by Kivixa.

3. LOCAL PROCESSING
On-Device AI: All AI analysis, document summarization, and chat interactions occur strictly on your device's CPU/GPU. No text or data is transmitted to the cloud for processing.

Native Engines: The Rust-based engines process data locally in your device's memory. No data is cached or sent externally.

4. THIRD-PARTY SERVICES
While Kivixa is local-first, you may interact with third-party services through:

GitHub/F-Droid/Winget: If you download updates, these platforms may collect standard technical metadata (IP address, device type) required for file delivery.

External Links: If you click a link within the app, you will be directed to an external site governed by its own privacy policy.

5. DATA SECURITY
Because your data is stored locally, its security depends on the security of your device. We recommend using encrypted storage, biometrics, or strong passwords to protect your device from unauthorized access.

6. CHILDREN'S PRIVACY
Kivixa does not knowingly collect data from anyone. Because all data stays on your device, we have no way to identify the age of our users. We encourage parents to monitor their children's device usage.

7. CONTACT INFORMATION
For any questions regarding these policies, please open an issue on our official GitHub repository.
